STATUS: fail

SUMMARY: One reproduced deviation from criterion 4: a 304 drops `Last-Modified`, which the criterion says must be kept. Everything else I probed held: the If-None-Match matrix matches `http.ServeContent` case for case, the wire behaviour for HEAD, 304 and Flush is correct, and Flush streams through `ResponseController`. The probe file is deleted and `git status` is back to `M README.md`, `A middleware/etag.go`, `A middleware/etag_test.go`.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probe `middleware/zz_probe_etag_test.go` was created and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] `writeNotModified` deletes `Last-Modified` (etag.go, `h.Del("Last-Modified")`). Criterion 4 says the 304 keeps "other headers" and drops only Content-Type, Content-Length and Content-Encoding. Reproduced with `go test -race ./middleware -run ZZPNotModifiedKeepsLastModified`: `middleware/zz_probe_etag_test.go:55: Last-Modified dropped on 304 (got ""); criterion keeps other headers`. Mitigation: `net/http`'s writeNotModified also drops it when an ETag is present, so the author may be mirroring it deliberately. The criterion text still contradicts the code, and `TestETagNotModifiedHeaders` locks in the removal. Orchestrator to decide; the fix is to drop that line and its assertion.
- [minor] A handler that sets `ETag` to an empty value (`w.Header()["ETag"] = []string{""}`) gets a computed tag written over it. Not reproduced against criterion 3 as written, since the header is arguably not "set"; noted only.
- [minor] Handler calls Flush after Hijack: Flush's `startStreaming` logs `http: response.WriteHeader on hijacked connection from ...etag.go:92`. This is handler misuse, and net/http's own Flush after hijack also misbehaves, so not a real finding.

CHECKS:
- `ZZPDiffIfNoneMatch` (23 If-None-Match inputs incl. `W/`, `"x"` vs `"xy"`/`"X"`, `,,`, `"abc`, `W/abc`, whitespace, trailing commas, list with leading `"a",`) vs `http.ServeContent` with same ETag → pass, all identical.
- `ZZPWire304` (real httptest server, `W/` request, 304) → pass: CL=0, no Content-Type, ETag kept, empty body.
- `ZZPWireHeadAndContentLength` (GET/HEAD, plain vs wrapped server) → pass: Content-Length and body semantics match plain net/http, HEAD body empty, ETag present.
- `ZZPFlushViaResponseControllerStreams` (real server; client must read "a" before handler continues) → pass: first byte arrived before the handler returned, no ETag.
- `ZZPWriteHeaderOrderAndFlushedStatus` (Flush, then WriteHeader(404)) → pass: status 200, same as net/http.
- `ZZPNotModifiedKeepsLastModified` → FAIL (the blocking finding above).
- Existing `etag_test.go` helpers and the `-race` concurrency test were read but not re-run; the orchestrator already ran them.
- README: `[ETag]` row and link are in the right positions; the row is 100 columns, same as its neighbours.

OPEN QUESTIONS: Should `Last-Modified` be dropped on 304 (net/http behaviour, contradicting criterion 4's literal wording) or kept (criterion)? This decides the blocking finding.
